question.worked_solution:
First, we substitute $u={x}^{3}-1.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=3{x}^{2}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to -\infty $ when $x\to -\infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u={x}^{3}-1$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $-\infty $ | $-2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-\infty $ | $-9$ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{-2}\frac{6{x}^{2}}{({x}^{3}-1)^{3}}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{-9}\frac{2}{{u}^{3}}\,\text{d}u
$$

Finally, we proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-9}\frac{2}{{u}^{3}}\,\text{d}u & =2{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-9}{u}^{-3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-2}]}_{a}^{-9} \\  & =-1\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}]}_{a}^{-9} \\  & =-1\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-9)^{2}}-\frac{1}{{a}^{2}}] \\  & =-1\cdot (\frac{1}{81}-0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{81}.\end{aligned}
$$
